text:
maria: Heads-up — customer RedwoodCorp (Private/VPC) reporting intermittent API 502s + TLS handshake failures when traffic traverses from eu-west-1 AZs -> us-east-1 services. Only affects some AZs, others fine. Started ~22:00 UTC after we rolled a small network change on their side.
maria: Quick clues from customer:
- app logs: half the requests show "TLS alert 40" / handshake fail
- curl -v shows cert CN mismatch for some requests
- they saw different A records from different AZs for the same internal hostname

maria: Paste of dig from a failing node (eu-west-1a):
```
$ dig +short internal-api.prod.redwood.internal @10.2.1.2
10.10.200.45
```

maria: And dig from a working node (eu-west-1c):
```
$ dig +short internal-api.prod.redwood.internal @10.2.1.2
10.50.10.9
```

maria: The IPs are in different region pools; customer says 10.10.200.45 resolves to us-east-1 NLB which has cert CN=us-east.internal. So correlation is DNS -> wrong region -> cert CN mismatch -> TLS fails.
alex: Thanks — are both VPCs associated with the same Route53 private hosted zone? Does the resolver have outbound endpoints in both regions?

maria: They confirmed the private hosted zone is associated with eu-west VPC only. There's a resolver endpoint in eu-west and a forwarding rule to us-east. Customer suspects the resolver sometimes forwards to public-facing fallback which returns us-east IPs.

raj: Possible causes: resolver fallthrough / conditional forwarder misconfig, stale cache in the resolver endpoints, or egress/firewall between AZs blocking return path so the resolver retries an alternative (public) path. Also check security groups on the resolver ENIs — if UDP/53 responses are blocked from us-east resolver IPs, it could trigger fallback.

jen: Can we get a tcpdump from a failing pod showing the DNS exchange + TLS handshake? Need to see whether the A reply is coming from the Route53 resolver IP or from an external recursor. Also confirm source port range — sometimes stateful firewall drops ephemeral replies.

maria: Customer ran tcpdump and attached minimal excerpt:
```
12:34:10.123456 IP 10.2.10.5.54321 > 10.2.1.2.53: 12345+ A? internal-api.prod.redwood.internal.
12:34:10.123457 IP 10.2.1.2.53 > 10.2.10.5.53: 12345 1/0/0 A 10.10.200.45
12:34:10.223000 IP 10.2.10.5.44321 > 10.10.200.45.443: Flags [S], seq 0
12:34:10.223100 IP 10.10.200.45.443 > 10.2.10.5.44321: Flags [RST]
```

maria: curl -v output from same node:
```
* TLS handshake, certificate subject: CN=us-east.internal
* SSL: certificate subject name 'us-east.internal' doesn't match requested host name 'internal-api.prod.redwood.internal'
```

alex: That tcpdump shows the resolver answered with the us-east IP. So the question is why the resolver returns that for some queries and not others. Two lines of investigation: check Route53 resolver rules/associations and check any network NAT/egress allowlist rules that might cause recursive lookups to go to public resolvers.

raj: Additionally, confirm that the application nodes are using the resolver in their region and not accidentally using a public resolver due to /etc/resolv.conf order. A restart of the resolver client or kube-dns could surface the bug if it's a caching issue.

jen: Workaround for customer (short-term): pin correct IP in app hosts file on affected nodes to eu-west NLB, or put an IP-based NetworkPolicy that forces traffic to eu-west endpoints. Not ideal but buys time.

maria: Customer applied hosts patch on two nodes and those nodes are back to green. They asked for permanent fix — want us to confirm cause and remediation steps.

ops-oncall: I'm opening an internal infra ticket: INFRA-12987 to verify resolver rules, endpoint health, and any conditional forwarders between eu-west and us-east. Also to check for any recent changes to firewall/NAT egress allowlists that match the time window.

support-bot: Incident created INFRA-12987 by @ops-oncall. Priority P2.

alex: Remediation plan we should propose to customer: 1) Verify Route53 private hosted zone associations include both VPCs (or use outbound resolver with a rule that prefers internal authoritative answers). 2) Ensure Route53 resolver endpoints are healthy in both regions and that SGs allow UDP/TCP 53 between app subnets and resolver ENIs. 3) Check egress/NAT IP allowlists on firewall appliances — add resolver ENI ranges if needed. 4) Clear resolver caches or restart kube-dns/coredns to avoid stale mappings. 5) As longer term, add health-aware DNS responses via split-horizon with failover mapping so cert/regional affinity is preserved.

raj: Also, check if client is doing EDNS(0) or TCP fallback — some middleboxes drop large UDP DNS responses and cause query fallthrough.

maria: I'll collect:
- dig +trace from failing/working nodes
- full tcpdump pcap
- list of resolver ENI IPs + SGs from customer
- time window logs when they rolled the change
I'll attach to INFRA-12987.

ops-oncall: Noted. For now I've asked customer to leave hosts patch on until we confirm fix. Please post results here when you have the trace and pcaps.

jen: If infra team confirms resolver misrouting, recommend a config change: create a conditional forwarder/Rule in the Route53 resolver that explicitly points queries for prod domain to the eu-west authoritative resolver, preventing fallthrough to public recursors.

maria: Thanks — will follow up with artifacts in the ticket. :thumbsup:

support-bot: Reminder: please set the incident channel if you want cross-team notifications.
